notes: Gates are attribute rules (OR over rules, AND within a rule). ungated_ledger_share above ~10% means the gate is wrong, not the location.

Gates widened 2026-09-19 after the ungated-ledger audit: the World Builder attributes bunds, drainage and small-stream water supply from wetland and moisture evidence that the displayed attributes cannot see, so those gates use terrain plus a humid-climate rule rather than the EU5 river level alone. envelope_quantile 0.5 keeps caps from overshooting the maximum for most locations; uncovered maximum is reported.

envelope_fit_scope: with_ledger fits each cap equation over gated locations that have ledger mass for that type (caps mean where works are historically attested; better start fit, larger maximum overshoot); gated fits over every eligible location (smaller overshoot, more starting works blocked by caps). The maximum map is only representable to the extent attributes explain it; overshoot versus uncovered maximum is the reported trade-off.
round_to: people per building level are rounded to the nearest multiple of this many people after the quantisation search.

Development enters each cap equation as one linear term, levels_per_development_point (EU5: add = { value = development multiply = gamma }), bounded by max_levels_per_development_point and rounded to 0.01; caps are floored to whole levels. The development map is read and hash-checked, never adjusted.

2026-09-19: 'continental' removed from the paddy-control gate. It had been added for northern Japan and Korea (3.5% of the maximum paddy ledger) but made 3,452 continental locations paddy-eligible, e.g. Stockholm with 11 cap levels at development 100; outside Asia those caps added 1.09B people to the world maximum. The Japanese and Korean continental paddy stays uncovered (leftover) instead.
2026-09-20: capacity_percent_per_point 0. Targets and ledger units are people directly; no development multiplier anywhere in the capacity model.

2026-09-20: development_levels_per_point_min sets a design floor on the development term of each cap equation (levels per point; the game starting development runs 0-45, so 0.06 means about +2.7 management levels at 45). The envelope fit may raise the term, never lower it below the floor. Development multiplies nothing else.

2026-09-20: caps are compared with the physical maximum at each location's own starting development (columns *_cap; fit "maximum"); *_cap_at_reference evaluates the cap equation at maximum_reference_development (45, the highest game starting value) and is informational (fit "maximum_at_reference_development"). No cap is evaluated at development 100 any more.

2026-09-20: capacity_percent_per_point 0.01 = the EU5 engine's own development multiplier (1% per point, not scriptable away); development is the vanilla game-start value computed from the vanilla rules (data/raw/vanilla/start_development_1337.csv, range 0..~110).
2026-09-20: development floors halved for the vanilla 0..110 range (management 0.03 levels per point = +3 levels at 100); maximum_reference_development 100.

2026-09-20: engine development multiplier observed in game as 2.5% per point (Zhigu: development 36 -> Population Capacity +90%); capacity_percent_per_point 0.025. Not a scriptable value; no define found.
allow_failed_development_checks_reason: 2026-09-20: development is the game starting value (configs/development.json source.kind game_start); its sanity suite is informational and never gates.

oasis_irrigation.note: Water-supply ledger of dry locations without surface water in the displayed attributes: qanats, wells and oasis channels.

pastoral.note: Natural capacity times the pastoral land share (World Builder pastoral_area_ha / area), carved out of the natural target; no expansion at maximum. Tested 2026-09-19 and disabled: carving 58M people of pastoral land out of the natural target lowered the start-model fit (R2 0.831 -> 0.812, median error 25% -> 30%) because the class-level caps of a pastoral building cannot return the carved mass per location. Building type kept for later use.
